Detailed Description

Dynamic array based on segments of exponentially growing size.

This array is able to grow dynamically upon request, without any reallocation.

The grow operation involves an allocation of a new array segment, without reallocating the already used memory, and thus not increasing the heap fragmentation. This also implies that the address of the stored elements never changes.

Allocated segments grow in size exponentially.

◆ tommy_array_clear()

void tommy_array_clear ( tommy_array *  array)

Removes all elements, preserving the allocated capacity.

Call tommy_array_shrink() after clearing to restore the initial capacity. Pointed-to elements are not freed. The array remains initialized and can be reused immediately.

)

Exchanges two initialized arrays without copying their elements.

Element references remain valid and belong to the other array. Passing the same array twice has no effect.

Parameters
firstThe first array.
secondThe second array.
Note
This operation is O(1).

◆ tommy_array_foreach()

TOMMY_API void tommy_array_foreach ( tommy_array *  array,
tommy_foreach_func *  func 
)

Calls the specified function for each element in the array.

You cannot add or remove elements, nor change the size of the array, from inside the callback.

If the callback frees the elements, the array retains dangling pointers. Call tommy_array_clear() before reusing it, or tommy_array_done() to release its storage.

Parameters
arrayThe array.
funcFunction to call with each element.
